docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The block diagram shows the main electrical components and signal connections for the GripRx motor board. It identifies the power sources, microcontroller inputs and outputs, actuator control, limit switches, and the interface with the Force Board.

The system uses a Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano as the main microcontroller. Two Omron D2F-01L limit switches provide the home and end position signals to digital inputs RD2 and RD3. The PIC controls the Texas Instruments DRV8871DDAR H-Bridge Driver using a PWM signal from RB3 and a direction signal from RD1. The H-Bridge drives the DFRobot FIT0492-A gear motor.

The motor side is powered by a 9 V, 3 A power supply. A 5 V linear regulator is included for the regulated 5 V supply. Communication with the Force Board is provided through connector J1 using UART, FORCE_OK, FORCE_ANA, and ground connections.

docs.title: Component Selection – GripRx Motor Board
docs.text: Course: EGR 304 – Embedded Systems Design Team: 103 – GripRx Project: Motor Board

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this assignment is to evaluate and compare major electronic components for the GripRx Motor Board. The board uses a PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller to control a DC gear motor through an H-bridge motor driver.

The selection process considers electrical compatibility, performance, cost, power requirements, and ease of integration.

The major components evaluated are:

  1. DC Gear Motor
  2. H-Bridge Motor Driver
  3. 5V Voltage Regulator
  4. 9V Power Supply

docs.title: 1. DC Gear Motor Selection
docs.text:
Table 1: DC Gear Motor Comparison

Solution Pros Cons Option 1: DFRobot FIT0492-A Price: $11.90 each Voltage: 12V Speed: 50 RPM no-load Rated torque: 9 kg-cm Rated current: 0.68A Stall current: 2.19A Product Link - Lowest price among the compared motors - High rated torque for a geared motor - Low rotational speed suitable for controlled gripping - Metal gearbox for mechanical durability - Requires a 12V supply for rated performance - Stall current exceeds the 1A current-limit target in the current block diagram - Relatively heavy at 210g - No integrated position encoder Option 2: Pololu 50:1 37D Price: $38.95 each Voltage: 12V Speed: 200 RPM no-load Stall torque: 21 kg-cm (extrapolated) Stall current: 5.5A Product Link - Durable metal gearbox - Higher speed for faster movement - Optional encoder-equipped version - Detailed manufacturer specifications - More expensive than Option 1 - High stall current requires careful driver and power-supply selection - Higher speed may require additional control for precise gripping - Extrapolated stall torque is not a recommended continuous operating torque Option 3: Pololu 150:1 Micro Listed price: $26.45 each Voltage: 12V Speed: 200 RPM no-load Stall torque: approximately 2.9 kg-cm Stall current: 0.8A Product Link - Compact and lightweight design - Lower stall current than the other two motors - Metal gearbox - Easier to accommodate in a small mechanism - Much lower stall torque than the other options - May not provide enough force for the gripping mechanism - Higher no-load speed than Option 1 - More expensive than Option 1

Preliminary Choice: Option 1 – DFRobot FIT0492-A Metal DC Gear Motor.

Rationale: The DFRobot FIT0492-A is the preferred preliminary choice because it provides a useful combination of low output speed, substantial rated torque, and low cost. Its rated torque of 9 kg-cm and rated current of 0.68A make it a promising candidate for the GripRx gripping mechanism. The 50 RPM no-load speed may also help provide controlled opening and closing movement. Compared with the Pololu alternatives, it offers an attractive balance between torque and cost. However, the motor is rated for 12V, while the current block diagram specifies a 9V power supply. The power supply selection should therefore be reconsidered. Additionally, the motor has a stall current of 2.19A, which exceeds the currently proposed 1A motor-driver current limit. The team must evaluate the motor driver's current-limit setting and confirm that the motor can produce sufficient gripping force without overheating or stalling. The final motor selection will be confirmed after the mechanical design is completed and the required gripping torque is calculated or measured.

Sources: - DFRobot FIT0492-A Manufacturer Specifications - Pololu 50:1 Metal Gearmotor Specifications - Pololu 150:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor Listing
